subject: Cloudway RFI: runrate validation & quantization-fit assessment
messages:

Subject: Cloudway RFI: runrate validation & quantization-fit assessment

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for taking this RFI. We're assembling answers to a dedicated capacity sizing questionnaire and need concrete guidance on GPU families, mixed-precision / INT8 fit, and reservation sizing for our production inference use cases. High-level background:
- Models: 13B instruction-tuned chat model + a 70B customer-rewrite model for longer context.
- Target traffic: steady-state ~18k requests/day (avg payload ~400 tokens), with burst windows that could double that during product launches.
- Latency SLOs: p50 ~ <60ms, p95 < 350ms for chat flows.
- Desired runrate: planning for 6 months runway with committed capacity; want guidance on baseline commit + burst lanes.

Please see attached Cloudway_questionnaire.xlsx (we've populated some usage numbers) and confirm what committed GPU mix (H100 | A100 | L4) and quantization options you'd recommend. Also include estimated throughput and token/sec numbers we can use for procurement.

Procurement timeline: draft SOW and indicative pricing by Oct 14 would be ideal.

Thanks,
Aisha Khan
Head of Platform, Cloudway AI
procure@cloudway.ai

Attachment: Cloudway_questionnaire.xlsx (referenced)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-11T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Cloudway RFI: runrate validation & quantization-fit assessment

Hi Aisha — thanks for the clear RFI and the populated worksheet. Attaching our Dedicated sizing workbook (redwood-dedicated-sizing-workbook-v2.xlsx) and a quick GPU profile CSV with estimate points. High level answers up front:

- Suggested committed baseline: equivalent of 4x H100-80GB (model mix dependent). This covers steady-state chat + the 70B rewrite model at conservative batching.
- Burst lane: ability to burst to 8x H100-equivalent for launch peaks (short windows, pre-warmed containers).
- Quantization guidance: for the 13B chat model we recommend FP16 or BF16 for lowest latency with minimal quality impact; INT8 can be offered for the 13B only as an opt-in (saves ~2.5x memory, 1.6-2x throughput uplift, but requires evals). 70B: recommend FP16/BF16 or 4-bit quantized configs with validation; full INT8 for 70B has higher risk for quality regressions.
- Throughput estimates (typical): one H100-80GB can sustain ~250–350 concurrent chat requests (400 tokens avg) under optimized batching and KV caching; approximate token throughput 20k–30k tokens/sec per H100 in mixed workloads.
- Latency and batching: to meet p95 < 350ms we recommend short batching windows (3–6ms) and aggressive KV prefix cache for frequent prompts.

I've left detailed worksheets with per-model token/sec, tail-latency assumptions, and slotting options in the attached workbook. Can we schedule 30 minutes tomorrow to walk through the workbook and a short mutual action plan (SOW / milestone draft)?

Regards,
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai
Attachment: redwood-dedicated-sizing-workbook-v2.xlsx; gpu-profile-estimates.csv

Thanks, Soojin — that is helpful. A few follow-ups before the call:
1) Can you quantify the quality delta we should expect if we move 13B to INT8 for cost saving (sample acceptance metrics we'd expect to see)?
2) For the burst lane, do you recommend hot spares (always-on nodes) vs. on-demand cold spin-up with pre-warm hooks?
3) Procurement asks for a sample SOW and an indicative monthly committed cost estimate for the baseline.

Quick answers from our side: the 70B rewrite accounts for ~28% of inference requests but represents ~55% of token volume given longer sequences. Typical concurrency during peak launches is ~2.2x steady-state.

Can you include a short table with baseline committed configuration + expected p95 token latency and token/sec? If you can get that to us by EOD Oct 13 we'll be in a good spot for the procurement cadence.

Cheers,
Aisha
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@cloudway.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-12T14:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Cloudway RFI: runrate validation & quantization-fit assessment

Aisha — answers inline and a concise baseline table below. Attaching a short note on quantization tradeoffs (quantization-impact-note.pdf).

1) INT8 quality delta (13B): in our internal evals across 10 business-critical prompt families we observe an average BLEU/ROUGE-style surrogate drop of ~0.5–1.2 points; for instruction-following metrics, drop is typically <1%. For customer-facing metrics we recommend a blind A/B on a held prompt set before enabling INT8 in production.

2) Burst lane recommendation: hybrid approach. Keep 1–2 hot spares pre-warmed (maintain KV priming) for <10s scale-ups; allow on-demand cold spin-ups for larger longer-lived bursts (with pre-warm hooks to reduce cold-start latency). This keeps committed cost lower while achieving low-latency bursts.

3) Indicative monthly committed cost (ballpark): baseline 4x H100-equivalent reserved = $62,000/month (negotiable based on term & region); burst credits (factor) for up to 8x = additional $18k/month of committed burst allowance; on-demand overage at our published on-demand rates. We'll draft SOW with milestones and SLA targets.

Baseline configuration table (recommended):
- Baseline committed: 4x H100-80GB equivalent
  - Expected aggregate throughput: 80–110k tokens/sec
  - Expected p95 latency (chat, 400 tokens payload): 220–320ms (with 3–6ms batching windows & KV cache)
- Burst configuration: up to 8x H100-equivalent (hot spares 1–2 nodes)
  - Peak throughput: up to 180–220k tokens/sec
  - p95 latency in burst: 300–450ms (depends on cache hit rate)
- Alternative mixed-fleet: 2x H100 + 4x A100-80GB (cost-optimized)
  - Aggregate throughput: 60–90k tokens/sec
  - p95 latency: 250–380ms

Operational notes: continuous batching and prefix KV caching reduce cost by ~18–30% on steady state; kernel selection will prefer fused attention paths for the 70B model which the runtime selects automatically per-request.

Next steps: I'll follow up with the draft SOW and a small per-model MPT (model performance table) by EOD tomorrow (Oct 13).

Best,
Soojin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
